```{=html}
<script>
(function loadGSAP() {
  var savedDefine = window.define;
  window.define = undefined;
  var s1 = document.createElement('script');
  s1.src = 'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.5/gsap.min.js';
  s1.onload = function() {
    window.define = savedDefine;
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event('gsap-ready'));
  };
  s1.onerror = function() {
    window.define = savedDefine;
    document.dispatchEvent(new Event('gsap-ready'));
  };
  document.head.appendChild(s1);
})();
</script>

<style>
/* MaxDiff theater extras (scene specific bits, theater shell comes from styles.css) */
.md-rating-card { background:#faf6ef; border:1px solid rgba(44,62,80,0.15); border-radius:10px; padding:18px 22px; max-width:360px; margin:0 auto; box-shadow:0 4px 16px rgba(44,62,80,0.06); }
.md-rating-title { font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#2c3e50; font-size:1.05rem; margin-bottom:14px; }
.md-rating-track { position:relative; height:8px; background:rgba(44,62,80,0.12); border-radius:4px; margin:18px 4px 6px; }
.md-rating-fill { position:absolute; left:0; top:0; bottom:0; width:80%; background:linear-gradient(90deg,#b8945a,#2c3e50); border-radius:4px; }
.md-rating-thumb { position:absolute; top:50%; left:80%; width:18px; height:18px; background:#b8945a; border:2px solid #faf6ef; border-radius:50%; transform:translate(-50%,-50%); box-shadow:0 2px 6px rgba(44,62,80,0.25); }

.md-rating-caption { text-align:center; color:#888; font-style:italic; font-size:0.88rem; margin-top:12px; }

.md-grid-4 { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:14px; max-width:540px; margin:0 auto; }
.md-card { background:#faf6ef; border:1px solid rgba(44,62,80,0.18); border-radius:8px; padding:14px 16px; position:relative; min-height:90px; display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(44,62,80,0.05); }
.md-card-code { font-size:0.72rem; letter-spacing:0.1em; color:#b8945a; text-transform:uppercase; margin-bottom:6px; }
.md-card-name { font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#2c3e50; font-size:0.95rem; line-height:1.25; }
.md-stamp { position:absolute; top:-12px; right:-12px; width:48px; height:48px; border-radius:50%; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; font-weight:700; font-size:0.72rem; color:#faf6ef; box-shadow:0 3px 8px rgba(44,62,80,0.18); opacity:0; transform:scale(0); }
.md-stamp-best { background:#5a8a5a; }
.md-stamp-worst { background:#7a3a3a; }

.md-figs-grid { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(11,1fr); gap:6px; max-width:520px; margin:0 auto; }
.md-fig { width:100%; aspect-ratio:1/2; background:#2c3e50; border-radius:3px 3px 6px 6px; opacity:0; }
.md-figs-caption { text-align:center; color:#888; font-style:italic; font-size:0.88rem; margin-top:18px; }
.md-figs-totals { display:flex; justify-content:center; gap:32px; margin-top:14px; font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#2c3e50; }
.md-figs-totals .num { font-size:1.5rem; font-weight:700; color:#b8945a; }
.md-figs-totals .lbl { font-size:0.78rem; letter-spacing:0.08em; color:#888; text-transform:uppercase; }

.md-anchor-pair { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr auto 1fr; gap:24px; align-items:center; max-width:600px; margin:0 auto; }
.md-anchor-vs { font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#888; font-style:italic; }
.md-card-mystery { background:repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,#faf6ef,#faf6ef 6px,#f0ead8 6px,#f0ead8 12px); border-style:dashed; }
.md-card-mystery .md-card-name { color:#b8945a; font-size:2rem; text-align:center; }

.md-cbar-row { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; max-width:560px; margin:0 auto 8px; }
.md-cbar-lbl { font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#2c3e50; font-size:0.85rem; min-width:80px; text-align:right; }
.md-cbar-track { flex:1; height:18px; background:rgba(44,62,80,0.06); border-radius:3px; overflow:hidden; }
.md-cbar-fill { height:100%; background:#2c3e50; width:0; border-radius:3px; }

.md-utility-cards { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr); gap:10px; max-width:600px; margin:0 auto; }
.md-util-card { background:#faf6ef; border:1px solid rgba(44,62,80,0.18); border-radius:8px; padding:10px 8px; text-align:center; position:relative; }
.md-util-code { font-size:0.65rem; letter-spacing:0.08em; color:#b8945a; text-transform:uppercase; margin-bottom:4px; }
.md-util-name { font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#2c3e50; font-size:0.78rem; line-height:1.2; min-height:34px; }
.md-util-beta { font-family:'Cambria Math','STIX Two Math', Georgia, serif; font-style:italic; color:#b8945a; font-size:0.92rem; margin-top:6px; opacity:0; }
.md-util-prob-row { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr); gap:10px; max-width:600px; margin:10px auto 0; }
.md-util-prob-track { height:8px; background:rgba(44,62,80,0.08); border-radius:3px; overflow:hidden; }
.md-util-prob-fill { height:100%; width:0; background:#b8945a; border-radius:3px; }
.md-util-prob-val { font-size:0.74rem; color:#2c3e50; text-align:center; margin-top:3px; font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; }

.md-bayes-canvas { max-width:540px; margin:0 auto; position:relative; }
.md-bayes-svg { width:100%; height:220px; display:block; }
.md-bayes-caption { text-align:center; color:#888; font-style:italic; font-size:0.88rem; margin-top:12px; }

.md-three-panel { display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr); gap:18px; max-width:760px; margin:0 auto; }
.md-tp-title { font-family:'Playfair Display', Georgia, serif; color:#2c3e50; text-align:center; font-size:0.92rem; margin-bottom:10px; }
.md-tp-bar { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:6px; margin-bottom:4px; }
.md-tp-lbl { font-size:0.65rem; color:#888; min-width:24px; text-align:right; }
.md-tp-track { flex:1; height:8px; background:rgba(44,62,80,0.06); border-radius:2px; overflow:hidden; }
.md-tp-fill { height:100%; width:0; background:#2c3e50; border-radius:2px; }
.md-tp-cap { text-align:center; color:#888; font-style:italic; font-size:0.82rem; margin-top:14px; }

.md-note-page { background:#faf6ef; border:1px solid rgba(184,148,90,0.4); border-left:4px solid #b8945a; border-radius:4px; padding:22px 26px; max-width:480px; margin:0 auto; font-family:'Kalam', cursive; color:#2c3e50; line-height:1.7; box-shadow:0 4px 14px rgba(44,62,80,0.06); }
.md-note-page ol { padding-left:24px; margin:0; }

@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .md-grid-4 { grid-template-columns:1fr; }

<script>
function initMaxDiffTheater() {
  var hasGsap = typeof gsap !== 'undefined';

  var screen = document.getElementById('gs-md-screen');
  var tlFill = document.getElementById('gs-md-tl-fill');
  var prevBtn = document.getElementById('gs-md-prev');
  var nextBtn = document.getElementById('gs-md-next');
  var counterEl = document.getElementById('gs-md-counter');
  var restartBtn = document.getElementById('gs-md-restart');
  var currentScene = 0;

  function clearScreen() {
    if (hasGsap) gsap.killTweensOf(screen.querySelectorAll('*'));
    screen.innerHTML = '';
    screen.style.opacity = 1;
  }
  function aFromTo(t, f, to) { if (hasGsap) gsap.fromTo(t, f, to); }
  function aTo(t, to) { if (hasGsap) gsap.to(t, to); }
  function aFrom(t, f) { if (hasGsap) gsap.from(t, f); }

  function showCharacter(src, text, side) {
    var wrap = document.createElement('div');
    wrap.className = 'gs-char-scene';
    var charHtml = '<div class="gs-char-big"><img src="' + src + '" alt="Persona" /></div>';
    var bubbleHtml = '<div class="gs-bubble"><div class="gs-bubble-tail"></div><p>' + text + '</p></div>';
    wrap.innerHTML = (side === 'right') ? (bubbleHtml + charHtml) : (charHtml + bubbleHtml);
    screen.appendChild(wrap);
    if (hasGsap) {
      var charEl = wrap.querySelector('.gs-char-big');
      var bubEl = wrap.querySelector('.gs-bubble');
      aFromTo(charEl,
        { xPercent: (side === 'right' ? 30 : -30), opacity: 0 },
        { xPercent: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.out',
          onComplete: function() { gsap.set(charEl, { clearProps: 'all' }); } });
      aFromTo(bubEl, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 0.3 });
      aTo(charEl.querySelector('img'), { y: -6, duration: 2, ease: 'sine.inOut', repeat: -1, yoyo: true, delay: 0.4 });
    }
  }

  var scenes = [
    // Scene 1: The problem with rating scales
    function() {
      screen.innerHTML = '<div class="gs-act-wrap">' +
        '<div class="gs-act-tag">Once upon a time</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-act-name">The trouble with rating scales</div>' +
        '<div class="md-rating-card" style="margin-top:18px;">' +
          '<div class="md-rating-title">MGTA 495 Marketing Analytics</div>' +
          '<div class="md-rating-track"><div class="md-rating-fill" id="md-rfill"></div><div class="md-rating-thumb" id="md-rthumb"></div></div>' +
          '<div class="md-rating-scale"><span>1</span><span>5</span><span>10</span></div>' +
          '<div class="md-rating-stars" id="md-rstars"></div>' +
        '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-rating-caption">Rate this class from 1 to 10. Everyone says 8. We learn nothing.</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-char-scene" style="margin-top:24px;">' +
          '<div class="gs-char-big"><img src="../../assets/persona-guide.svg" alt="Guide" /></div>' +
          '<div class="gs-bubble"><div class="gs-bubble-tail"></div><p>Humans are bad at numbers. But great at choices.</p></div>' +
        '</div>' +
      '</div>';
      var stars = document.getElementById('md-rstars');
      stars.innerHTML = '<span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span>&#9733;</span><span style="opacity:0.3;">&#9733;</span><span style="opacity:0.3;">&#9733;</span>';
      if (hasGsap) {
        var thumb = document.getElementById('md-rthumb');
        var fill = document.getElementById('md-rfill');
        var tl = gsap.timeline({ repeat: -1, yoyo: true });
        tl.to(thumb, { left: '60%', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut' });
        tl.to(thumb, { left: '95%', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut' });
        tl.to(thumb, { left: '70%', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut' });
        var tl2 = gsap.timeline({ repeat: -1, yoyo: true });
        tl2.to(fill, { width: '60%', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut' });
        tl2.to(fill, { width: '95%', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut' });
        tl2.to(fill, { width: '70%', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut' });
        aFromTo('.gs-char-scene .gs-char-big', { xPercent: -20, opacity: 0 }, { xPercent: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.6, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 0.6 });
        aFromTo('.gs-char-scene .gs-bubble', { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, delay: 0.9 });
      }
    },
    // Scene 2: MaxDiff to the rescue (4 cards, best and worst stamps)
    function() {
      screen.innerHTML = '<div class="gs-act-wrap">' +
        '<div class="gs-act-tag">Every day</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-act-name">Pick the best. Pick the worst.</div>' +
        '<div class="md-grid-4" style="margin-top:18px;">' +
          '<div class="md-card md-c1"><div class="md-card-code">MGTA 453</div><div class="md-card-name">Business Analytics</div><div class="md-stamp md-stamp-best md-s1">BEST</div></div>' +
          '<div class="md-card md-c2"><div class="md-card-code">MGTA 451</div><div class="md-card-name">Marketing / Finance / Ops</div></div>' +
          '<div class="md-card md-c3"><div class="md-card-code">MGTA 464</div><div class="md-card-name">SQL</div></div>' +
          '<div class="md-card md-c4"><div class="md-card-code">MGTA 457</div><div class="md-card-name">Biz. Intelligence Systems</div><div class="md-stamp md-stamp-worst md-s2">WORST</div></div>' +
        '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-rating-caption" style="margin-top:18px;">Repeat the choice across many four-item screens. Preferences emerge from the pattern.</div>' +
      '</div>';
      if (hasGsap) {
        aFromTo('.md-grid-4 .md-card', { y: 24, opacity: 0 }, { y: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.12, ease: 'back.out(1.2)' });
        aFromTo('.md-s1', { scale: 0, opacity: 0, rotate: -20 }, { scale: 1, opacity: 1, rotate: -8, duration: 0.55, delay: 1.0, ease: 'back.out(2)' });
        aFromTo('.md-s2', { scale: 0, opacity: 0, rotate: 25 }, { scale: 1, opacity: 1, rotate: 12, duration: 0.55, delay: 1.4, ease: 'back.out(2)' });
      }
    },
    // Scene 3: The survey at scale (figures)
    function() {
      var figs = '';
      for (var i = 0; i < 88; i++) figs += '<div class="md-fig md-f' + i + '"></div>';
      screen.innerHTML = '<div class="gs-act-wrap">' +
        '<div class="gs-act-tag">Every day, continued</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-act-name">The survey at scale</div>' +
        '<div class="md-figs-grid" style="margin-top:18px;">' + figs + '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-figs-totals">' +
          '<div><div class="num" id="md-tot-r">0</div><div class="lbl">students</div></div>' +
          '<div><div class="num" id="md-tot-t">0</div><div class="lbl">tasks each</div></div>' +
          '<div><div class="num" id="md-tot-c">0</div><div class="lbl">choices</div></div>' +
        '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-figs-caption">85 students. 15 tasks each. 1,275 choices to learn from.</div>' +
      '</div>';
      if (hasGsap) {
        aFromTo('.md-fig', { y: -10, opacity: 0 }, { y: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.35, stagger: { each: 0.012, from: 'random' }, ease: 'power2.out' });
        var t1 = { v: 0 }, t2 = { v: 0 }, t3 = { v: 0 };
        var el1 = document.getElementById('md-tot-r'), el2 = document.getElementById('md-tot-t'), el3 = document.getElementById('md-tot-c');
        aTo(t1, { v: 85, duration: 1.0, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 1.0, onUpdate: function() { el1.textContent = Math.round(t1.v); } });
        aTo(t2, { v: 15, duration: 1.0, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 1.2, onUpdate: function() { el2.textContent = Math.round(t2.v); } });
        aTo(t3, { v: 1275, duration: 1.3, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 1.4, onUpdate: function() { el3.textContent = Math.round(t3.v).toLocaleString(); } });
      }
    },
    // Scene 4: The anchor
    function() {
      screen.innerHTML = '<div class="gs-act-wrap">' +
        '<div class="gs-act-tag">One day</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-act-name">The mystery item</div>' +
        '<div class="md-anchor-pair" style="margin-top:24px;">' +
          '<div class="md-card md-acard"><div class="md-card-code">MGTA 495</div><div class="md-card-name">Marketing Analytics</div></div>' +
          '<div class="md-anchor-vs">vs</div>' +
          '<div class="md-card md-card-mystery md-acard"><div class="md-card-name">?</div></div>' +
        '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-rating-caption" style="margin-top:18px;">Some screens compared a class to a mystery anchor. We will use it as the reference point.</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-char-scene" style="margin-top:22px;">' +
          '<div class="gs-bubble"><div class="gs-bubble-tail"></div><p>An anchor lets every class be measured against the same baseline.</p></div>' +
          '<div class="gs-char-big"><img src="../../assets/persona-analyst.svg" alt="Analyst" /></div>' +
        '</div>' +
      '</div>';
      if (hasGsap) {
        aFromTo('.md-anchor-pair .md-acard', { y: 20, opacity: 0 }, { y: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.18, ease: 'power2.out' });
        aFromTo('.md-anchor-vs', { scale: 0, opacity: 0 }, { scale: 1, opacity: 1, duration: 0.45, delay: 0.5, ease: 'back.out(1.6)' });
        aFromTo('.gs-char-scene .gs-char-big', { xPercent: 20, opacity: 0 }, { xPercent: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.6, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 0.9 });
        aFromTo('.gs-char-scene .gs-bubble', { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, delay: 1.2 });
      }
    },
    // Scene 5: Counts
    function() {
      var labels = ['MGTA 495','MGTA 455','MGTA 453','MGTA 451','MGTA 444'];
      var widths = [78, 64, 55, 42, 33];
      var rows = '';
      for (var i = 0; i < labels.length; i++) {
        rows += '<div class="md-cbar-row">' +
                  '<div class="md-cbar-lbl">' + labels[i] + '</div>' +
                  '<div class="md-cbar-track"><div class="md-cbar-fill md-cbf-' + i + '" data-w="' + widths[i] + '"></div></div>' +
                '</div>';
      }
      screen.innerHTML = '<div class="gs-act-wrap">' +
        '<div class="gs-act-tag">Because of that</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-act-name">Method one: counts</div>' +
        '<div style="margin-top:18px;">' + rows + '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-rating-caption" style="margin-top:18px;">Count how often each class was picked best, minus how often it was picked worst.</div>' +
      '</div>';
      if (hasGsap) {
        for (var k = 0; k < widths.length; k++) {
          (function(idx) {
            var el = document.querySelector('.md-cbf-' + idx);
            aTo(el, { width: widths[idx] + '%', duration: 0.9, ease: 'power2.out', delay: 0.2 + idx * 0.15 });
          })(k);
        }
      }
    },
    // Scene 6: MNL soft-max
    function() {
      var classes = [
        { code:'MGTA 453', name:'Business Analytics', prob: 0.42 },
        { code:'MGTA 444', name:'Analytics Consulting', prob: 0.28 },
        { code:'MGTA 452', name:'Large Data', prob: 0.20 },
        { code:'MGTA 457', name:'BI Systems', prob: 0.10 }
      ];
      var cards = '', probs = '';
      for (var i = 0; i < classes.length; i++) {
        var c = classes[i];
        cards += '<div class="md-util-card md-uc-' + i + '">' +
                   '<div class="md-util-code">' + c.code + '</div>' +
                   '<div class="md-util-name">' + c.name + '</div>' +
                   '<div class="md-util-beta md-ub-' + i + '">exp(&beta;<sub>' + (i+1) + '</sub>)</div>' +
                 '</div>';
        probs += '<div><div class="md-util-prob-track"><div class="md-util-prob-fill md-pf-' + i + '" data-w="' + Math.round(c.prob*100) + '"></div></div>' +
                 '<div class="md-util-prob-val md-pv-' + i + '">0%</div></div>';
      }
      screen.innerHTML = '<div class="gs-act-wrap">' +
        '<div class="gs-act-tag">Because of that</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-act-name">Method two: the MNL soft-max</div>' +
        '<div class="md-utility-cards" style="margin-top:18px;">' + cards + '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-util-prob-row">' + probs + '</div>' +
        '<div class="md-rating-caption" style="margin-top:14px;">Each class gets a utility. Probability of being picked best is the soft-max over utilities.</div>' +
        '<div class="gs-char-scene" style="margin-top:18px;">' +
          '<div class="gs-char-big"><img src="../../assets/persona-guide.svg" alt="Guide" /></div>' +
          '<div class="gs-bubble"><div class="gs-bubble-tail"></div><p>Same model the conjoint analysts use. The MNL.</p></div>' +
        '</div>' +
      '</div>';
      if (hasGsap) {
        aFromTo('.md-utility-cards .md-util-card', { y: 18, opacity: 0 }, { y: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.45, stagger: 0.1, ease: 'power2.out' });
        aFromTo('.md-util-beta', { y: 8, opacity: 0 }, { y: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.4, stagger: 0.1, delay: 0.7 });
        for (var k = 0; k < classes.length; k++) {
          (function(idx, c) {
            var fill = document.querySelector('.md-pf-' + idx);
            var val = document.querySelector('.md-pv-' + idx);
            var counter = { v: 0 };
            aTo(fill, { width: Math.round(c.prob*100) + '%', duration: 0.9, delay: 1.2 + idx * 0.12, ease: 'power2.out' });
```

## Introduction

MaxDiff, also called Best Worst Scaling, is the marketing analyst's quiet little workhorse. Ask a respondent to rate ten things on a one to ten scale and almost everyone hovers between seven and nine. Ask them instead to pick the best and the worst from a short list, repeat the question across several screens with different combinations, and the underlying preferences start to separate cleanly. People are unreliable judges of intensity, but they are very reliable judges of order.

The data for this post comes from a MaxDiff survey of the ten core MSBA classes at UCSD Rady. Eighty five students filled it out. Each respondent saw fifteen screens, eight of them four-item MaxDiff tasks and seven of them two-item tasks pitting a real class against an unlabeled anchor (more on that anchor in a moment). The analysis goes through the same data three ways: a raw counts score, a maximum likelihood multinomial logit, and a Bayesian version of that same logit. The three methods should agree on the broad ranking, which is the reassuring part. They will disagree on how much one class is preferred over another and on how confident we are in any particular gap, which is where each method earns its keep.

```{python}
# Sanity check: every 4-item task has exactly one best and one worst; every 2-item task has exactly one best, no worst.
```

When I first loaded the data, something looked off. The label sheet listed ten classes but the choice file contained eleven items. Item 11 had no name and appeared only on the smaller two-option screens, always in position two. After a closer look, the pattern became clear: about half of each respondent's screens were standard four-item MaxDiff tasks, and the other half were two-item tasks pitting a real class against this unnamed anchor. The anchor never won, never lost, but was always there.

This is a deliberate design choice. An anchor item gives every real class the same baseline to measure against. Instead of throwing those screens away (which would mean losing roughly half the data), I kept them and use item 11 as the reference category. Every coefficient I estimate in the sections that follow has a clean interpretation: how preferred is this class, relative to the anchor.

## Counts Analysis

The counts score is the simplest preference number you can put on a MaxDiff item. For each class, take the share of screens where it was picked best, subtract the share of screens where it was picked worst, and you have a single signed score on a roughly minus-one to plus-one scale. A class that always wins lands near plus one, a class that always loses lands near minus one, and anything that splits down the middle hovers around zero. The score does no inference and no smoothing, but it is fast, intuitive, and a useful sanity check for the model-based methods that come later.

```{python}
items_sorted = sorted(ITEM_LABELS.keys())
rows = []
for j in items_sorted:
    shown = (df['Item'] == j).sum()
    best = ((df['Item'] == j) & (df['Response'] == 1)).sum()
    worst = ((df['Item'] == j) & (df['Response'] == -1)).sum()
    pct_best = best / shown if shown else 0
    pct_worst = worst / shown if shown else 0
    rows.append({
        'item': j,
        'label': ITEM_LABELS[j],
        'times_shown': int(shown),
        'times_best': int(best),
        'times_worst': int(worst),
        'pct_best': pct_best,
        'pct_worst': pct_worst,
        'score': pct_best - pct_worst
    })

counts_df = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values('score', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
```

```{python}
# Bootstrap CIs: resample respondents with replacement, recompute the score per item.
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=20260523)
respondents = df['Record ID'].unique()
n_boot = 1000

boot_scores = {j: np.zeros(n_boot) for j in items_sorted}
df_by_resp = {r: df[df['Record ID'] == r] for r in respondents}

for b in range(n_boot):
    sample_ids = rng.choice(respondents, size=len(respondents), replace=True)
    sample = pd.concat([df_by_resp[r] for r in sample_ids], ignore_index=True)
    for j in items_sorted:
        shown = (sample['Item'] == j).sum()
        if shown == 0:
            boot_scores[j][b] = 0
            continue
        best = ((sample['Item'] == j) & (sample['Response'] == 1)).sum()
        worst = ((sample['Item'] == j) & (sample['Response'] == -1)).sum()
        boot_scores[j][b] = (best - worst) / shown

ci_lo = {j: np.quantile(boot_scores[j], 0.025) for j in items_sorted}
ci_hi = {j: np.quantile(boot_scores[j], 0.975) for j in items_sorted}
```

## From MaxDiff Data to MNL Choices

The counts score gets you a ranking and a quick feel for the data, but it does not give you a model. The next step is to write down a probability statement for each choice a respondent made, then estimate the parameters that maximize the joint likelihood of all those choices. The standard tool for this is the multinomial logit, often called the MNL.

Give each class $j$ a utility coefficient $\beta_j$. On a four-item screen where the items $\{a, b, c, d\}$ were shown and the respondent picked $b$ as best, the model assigns probability

$$
\Pr(\text{best} = b \mid \{a,b,c,d\}) = \frac{\exp(\beta_b)}{\exp(\beta_a) + \exp(\beta_b) + \exp(\beta_c) + \exp(\beta_d)}.
$$

This is the soft-max over the four utilities. The respondent also tells us which item is worst. Given that $b$ has already been removed from consideration, the worst choice among the remaining three uses the same soft-max with the signs of the utilities flipped, because the worst item is the one that minimizes utility:

$$
\Pr(\text{worst} = c \mid \{a, c, d\}) = \frac{\exp(-\beta_c)}{\exp(-\beta_a) + \exp(-\beta_c) + \exp(-\beta_d)}.
$$

Each four-item task therefore contributes two MNL observations to the likelihood: one best-pick and one worst-pick on the reduced set. Each two-item anchor task contributes one observation, a best-pick over two items, since no worst was recorded.

One last bookkeeping detail. The soft-max is invariant to adding a constant to every utility, which means the parameters are not identified without a reference point. The cleanest reference here is the anchor item itself: we fix $\beta_{11} = 0$ and estimate the other ten coefficients freely. Each $\beta_j$ then has a direct interpretation as the log-odds of preferring class $j$ to the anchor.

```{python}
# Reshape the data into a list of task records, ready for the likelihood we will write in Phase 2.
task_records = []
for (rid, tid), grp in df.groupby(['Record ID', 'Task']):
    shown = grp['Item'].tolist()
    best_rows = grp[grp['Response'] == 1]
    worst_rows = grp[grp['Response'] == -1]
    best_item = int(best_rows['Item'].iloc[0]) if len(best_rows) else None
    worst_item = int(worst_rows['Item'].iloc[0]) if len(worst_rows) else None
    task_records.append({
        'task_type': '4item' if len(grp) == 4 else '2item',
        'shown': [int(x) for x in shown],
        'best': best_item,
        'worst': worst_item
    })

print(f"Total task records: {len(task_records)}")
print("First 3 records:")
for r in task_records[:3]:
    print(" ", r)
```

## MNL via Maximum Likelihood

Counts give us a ranking and a rough sense of preference intensity, but they do not let us speak the language of probabilities. Two classes with the same counts score might come from very different preference distributions, and counts have no model-based way to express uncertainty about a coefficient or a share. For that we need a generative choice model. The multinomial logit, MNL for short, gives every class its own hidden utility and says that the probability of picking any item is the soft-max of utilities over the items on screen.

The exact form of the likelihood was laid out in the previous section. Each four-item task contributes two MNL observations: the best pick is a soft-max over all four utilities, and the worst pick on the remaining three uses the same soft-max with every utility flipped in sign. Each two-item anchor task contributes one observation, the best pick between a real class and item 11. We pin the anchor's utility at zero ($\beta_{11} = 0$), which leaves ten free parameters and gives every estimated $\beta_j$ the same plain-English reading: how much more, or less, preferred is class $j$ than the anchor.

What follows is the recipe in code. First, the log-likelihood function written by hand. Second, a sanity check at $\beta = 0$ where the answer can be worked out on paper. Third, the optimizer call with the analytical gradient supplied so BFGS does not need to estimate one from finite differences. Fourth, standard errors from the inverse Hessian and shares of preference from a soft-max across all eleven items.

```{python}
import numpy as np

# Numerically stable log-sum-exp.
# Given a vector x, returns log(sum(exp(x))) without overflow.
def log_sum_exp(x):
    m = np.max(x)
    return m + np.log(np.sum(np.exp(x - m)))

# Build the full utility vector u where u[j-1] = beta_j for j = 1..10
# and u[10] = 0 for the anchor (item 11). Item ids in the data are
# 1-indexed, so item j sits at u[j-1].
def full_utility_vector(beta_10):
    return np.concatenate([beta_10, [0.0]])  # length 11

# Log-likelihood. beta_10 is a length-10 numpy array.
def log_likelihood(beta_10, tasks):
    u = full_utility_vector(beta_10)
    ll = 0.0
    for task in tasks:
        shown = task['shown']
        best = task['best']
        # Utilities for items shown on this screen.
        u_shown = np.array([u[j - 1] for j in shown])
        # log P(best = picked best)
        ll += u[best - 1] - log_sum_exp(u_shown)

        if task['task_type'] == '4item':
            worst = task['worst']
            # Worst pick is over the three remaining items after best is removed,
            # using flipped utilities (worst is the item that minimizes utility).
            shown_after_best = [j for j in shown if j != best]
            u_remaining_flipped = np.array([-u[j - 1] for j in shown_after_best])
            ll += (-u[worst - 1]) - log_sum_exp(u_remaining_flipped)
    return ll

# scipy.optimize.minimize minimizes, so we feed it the negative log-likelihood.
def neg_log_likelihood(beta_10, tasks):
    return -log_likelihood(beta_10, tasks)

# Analytical gradient. For each task, the gradient of the log-prob with respect
# to u_j is (1{j picked} minus prob_j) over the items in the set. Supplying
# this lets BFGS converge cleanly instead of relying on noisy finite differences.
def neg_log_likelihood_grad(beta_10, tasks):
    u = full_utility_vector(beta_10)
    g = np.zeros(11)
    for task in tasks:
        shown = task['shown']
        best = task['best']
        u_shown = np.array([u[j - 1] for j in shown])
        m = np.max(u_shown)
        probs = np.exp(u_shown - m); probs = probs / probs.sum()
        for k, j in enumerate(shown):
            g[j - 1] += (1.0 if j == best else 0.0) - probs[k]
        if task['task_type'] == '4item':
            worst = task['worst']
            shown_after_best = [j for j in shown if j != best]
            u_neg = np.array([-u[j - 1] for j in shown_after_best])
            m2 = np.max(u_neg)
            qprobs = np.exp(u_neg - m2); qprobs = qprobs / qprobs.sum()
            for k, j in enumerate(shown_after_best):
                g[j - 1] += -(1.0 if j == worst else 0.0) + qprobs[k]
    # Drop the anchor (item 11) entry since beta_11 is fixed at 0.
    return -g[:10]
```

```{python}
# Sanity check. At beta = 0 every utility is zero, so every probability is 1/k
# where k is the number of items on screen. A 4-item task contributes
# log(1/4) for the best pick plus log(1/3) for the worst pick on the remaining
# three. A 2-item task contributes log(1/2). We can compute the expected total
# in closed form and check that the function matches.
n_4 = sum(1 for t in task_records if t['task_type'] == '4item')
n_2 = sum(1 for t in task_records if t['task_type'] == '2item')
expected_ll_at_zero = n_4 * (np.log(1/4) + np.log(1/3)) + n_2 * np.log(1/2)
computed_ll_at_zero = log_likelihood(np.zeros(10), task_records)

print(f"4-item tasks: {n_4}, 2-item tasks: {n_2}")
print(f"Expected log-likelihood at beta = 0: {expected_ll_at_zero:.4f}")
print(f"Computed log-likelihood at beta = 0: {computed_ll_at_zero:.4f}")
print(f"Difference: {abs(computed_ll_at_zero - expected_ll_at_zero):.2e}")
assert abs(computed_ll_at_zero - expected_ll_at_zero) < 0.01, "Sanity check failed."
print("Sanity check passed.")
```

```{python}
from scipy.optimize import minimize

# Start from zero (no preference difference vs anchor). BFGS will walk uphill
# in log-likelihood and build up an approximate inverse Hessian along the way,
# which we use to read off the standard errors.
result = minimize(
    fun=neg_log_likelihood,
    x0=np.zeros(10),
    args=(task_records,),
    jac=neg_log_likelihood_grad,
    method='BFGS',
    options={'gtol': 1e-6, 'disp': False}
)

beta_hat = result.x
neg_ll_at_opt = result.fun
ll_at_opt = -neg_ll_at_opt
hess_inv = result.hess_inv
se = np.sqrt(np.diag(hess_inv))

print(f"Converged: {result.success}")
print(f"Iterations: {result.nit}")
print(f"Log-likelihood at optimum: {ll_at_opt:.2f}")
print(f"Max |gradient| at optimum: {np.max(np.abs(result.jac)):.2e}")
print(f"Improvement over beta = 0: {ll_at_opt - expected_ll_at_zero:.2f}")
print()
print("Estimated coefficients (beta_11 = 0 by construction):")
for j in range(10):
    print(f"  beta_{j+1:2d} = {beta_hat[j]:+.4f}   SE = {se[j]:.4f}")
```

Two things are worth noting in the output. The first is that BFGS reports `Converged: False`. This is a quirk of the SciPy implementation, not a real problem. The line search stops once the step size hits the floating-point precision floor, even when the gradient is essentially zero. The diagnostics that actually matter all check out: the log-likelihood improved by more than 230 points over the null, the maximum absolute gradient at the reported optimum is on the order of $10^{-6}$, and the standard errors (around 0.13) sit in the range we would expect for 1,275 observations and ten parameters. The second is that every standard error is comfortably below half the coefficient, so all ten classes are estimated to differ from the anchor at well beyond conventional significance levels. That is what we want: the survey actually identifies preferences, not just noise.

Now convert utilities to shares of preference. The interpretation is the cleanest summary the MNL offers: if all eleven items appeared on a single screen and a respondent had to pick the best, the share of picks each item would attract is the soft-max of its utility over the sum of soft-maxes.

```{python}
# Shares of preference. Plain-English interpretation: if all 11 items appeared
# on one screen and the respondent had to pick the best, what fraction of
# picks would each item attract? This is the soft-max across all 11 utilities,
# with the anchor's utility fixed at 0.
u_full = np.concatenate([beta_hat, [0.0]])
shares = np.exp(u_full) / np.sum(np.exp(u_full))

# Print sorted descending for a quick read
order = np.argsort(-shares)
print("Shares of preference (sorted, anchor flagged):")
for k in order:
    item_id = k + 1
    flag = "  (anchor)" if item_id == 11 else ""
    print(f"  Item {item_id:2d}  {ITEM_LABELS[item_id]:42s}  {shares[k]*100:5.2f}%{flag}")
```

```{python}
# Results table for the post
mle_rows = []
for j in range(1, 12):
    if j <= 10:
        b = beta_hat[j - 1]
        s = se[j - 1]
        b_disp = f"{b:+.3f}"
        s_disp = f"{s:.3f}"
```

Finally, a side-by-side comparison of the MLE ranking with the counts ranking from earlier. Both methods rank the same data; any movement is interesting precisely because the two estimators weight the evidence differently.

```{python}
# Compare MLE ranking to the counts ranking from earlier.
# counts_df was built in the Counts Analysis section, sorted by score desc.
counts_rank_map = {row['item']: i + 1 for i, row in counts_df.iterrows()}
mle_rank_map = {row['item']: i + 1 for i, row in mle_df.iterrows()}

cmp_rows = []
for j in sorted(ITEM_LABELS.keys()):
    cr = counts_rank_map[j]
    mr = mle_rank_map[j]
    cmp_rows.append({
        'item': j,
        'label': ITEM_LABELS[j],
        'counts_rank': cr,
        'mle_rank': mr,
        'delta': mr - cr
    })

cmp_df = pd.DataFrame(cmp_rows).sort_values('mle_rank').reset_index(drop=True)

html = '<div style="overflow-x:auto;"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:0.88rem;">'
html += '<thead><tr style="background:#2c3e50;color:#faf6ef;">'
for col in ['Class', 'Counts rank', 'MLE rank', 'Move']:
    html += f'<th style="padding:10px 12px;text-align:left;">{col}</th>'
html += '</tr></thead><tbody>'
for i, row in cmp_df.iterrows():
    bg = '#f5efe6' if i % 2 == 0 else '#faf6ef'
    anchor = (row['item'] == 11)
    name_style = 'font-style:italic;color:#b8945a;' if anchor else ''
    delta = row['delta']
    if delta == 0:
        delta_disp = '<span style="color:#888;">no change</span>'
    elif delta < 0:
        delta_disp = f'<span style="color:#5a8a5a;">+{-delta} (up)</span>'
    else:
        delta_disp = f'<span style="color:#7a3a3a;">-{delta} (down)</span>'
    html += f'<tr style="background:{bg};">'
    html += f'<td style="padding:7px 12px;{name_style}">{row["label"]}{"  (reference)" if anchor else ""}</td>'
    html += f'<td style="padding:7px 12px;">{row["counts_rank"]}</td>'
    html += f'<td style="padding:7px 12px;">{row["mle_rank"]}</td>'
    html += f'<td style="padding:7px 12px;">{delta_disp}</td>'
    html += '</tr>'
html += '</tbody></table></div>'
HTML(html)
```

## MNL via Bayesian Estimation

Same model, different inference. Instead of point estimates and Hessian-based standard errors, the Bayesian view treats each beta as a random variable and returns a full posterior distribution. Coming soon: a random walk Metropolis-Hastings sampler with a weakly informative prior, trace plots, and credible intervals on the shares of preference.

## Comparing the Three Methods

Three methods, one set of preferences. Here we put the counts ranking, the MLE shares, and the Bayesian posterior shares side by side, see where they agree (almost always at the extremes), and where they disagree (almost always in the middle). Coming soon.
